source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: names and divisions read on the block image of the News-Letter's nomination list of 8 May 1924

note: Triennial election of the nineteen district electoral divisions of Kilkeel rural district, one member each. Ten candidates (all Unionists) were nominated on 7 May 1924 and returned unopposed; in the remaining nine (Nationalist) divisions no nominations were received (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924; Newry Reporter, 8 May 1924, p. 5: Attical, Bryansford, Cross, Drumreagh, Fofanny, Greencastle, Kilkeel North, Killowen, Lisnacree). These were treated as casual vacancies for the council to fill, not returns: at the annual meeting the council co-opted three additional members (A. Gordon, J.P., Humphrey Fry and John Randall) and deferred 'the filling of the casual vacancies in the nine electoral divisions for which no persons were elected' to its next meeting (Belfast News-Letter, 14 June 1924, p. 5). Co-options, not elections; who filled the nine divisions is not traced (round2-down, 7 Nov 2026). Sole nomination (Unionist). Returned unopposed.
